steps.tx: **Post streptococcal glomerulonephritis** follows nephritogenic pyogenes strains after throat (one to two weeks) or skin (impetigo, three to six weeks) infection: planted streptococcal antigens (SpeB and NAPlr debated) trigger complement alternative activation, subepithelial humps, low C3, smoky urine, oedema and hypertension in school children, mostly resolving, C3 normalising by six to eight weeks.
steps.say: Smoky urine, low C3, recent impetigo: PSGN timing separates throat from skin by weeks.

right.title: PSGN evidence
points: Anti DNase B best serology (skin source)
Throat or skin cultures often cleared

steps.tx: **Nephritogenicity** is strain property (M types 12 throat, 49 skin classics) plus host complement terrain, which is why only some pyogenes infections injure kidneys and family clusters occur in outbreaks. Antibiotic treatment of the index infection does not reliably prevent PSGN (unlike rheumatic fever), changing counselling honestly.
steps.say: Treating the throat prevents rheumatic fever; kidney protection is promised less honestly.

left.title: Strain and host
points: Planted antigen and in situ complex theories

right.title: Course expectations
points: C3 recovers by 8 weeks (persistent low: other diagnosis)
Epidemic control treats cases and contacts

steps.tx: **Streptococcus agalactiae** (group B streptococcus, GBS) is beta or non haemolytic, CAMP positive, hippurate hydrolysing, colonising vagina and gut of a fifth to a third of women, causing neonatal early onset sepsis and meningitis (prevention by intrapartum prophylaxis), late onset disease, and invasive disease in pregnancy, diabetes and old age.
steps.say: A colonised birth canal plus no prophylaxis equals neonatal sepsis arithmetic.

left.title: GBS identity
points: Beta haemolysis variable, some non haemolytic
Capsular types Ia to IX (III meningitis leaning)

right.title: GBS disease
points: Elderly and diabetic invasive disease rising

steps.tx: **Streptococcus agalactiae**, also called group B streptococcus, is beta or non haemolytic, CAMP positive, and hippurate hydrolysing. It colonises the vagina and gut of roughly a fifth to a third of women. At birth that colonisation can seed early onset neonatal sepsis and meningitis unless intrapartum prophylaxis is given. Late onset disease also occurs, and invasive infection appears in pregnancy, diabetes, and old age.
steps.say: Group B streptococcus colonises vagina and gut in many women and is CAMP positive. Without intrapartum prophylaxis that carriage becomes early neonatal sepsis and meningitis, with later disease in infants, pregnancy, diabetes, and older adults.

vis.alt: A diagram traces group B streptococci from a colonised vagina across birth into early neonatal sepsis.
vis.caption: Colonising streptococci in the birth canal are shown passing to a newborn who then develops early sepsis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Intrapartum prophylaxis** prevents early onset GBS: universal rectovaginal screening at 36 to 37 weeks (or risk based strategies in some countries), penicillin (ampicillin, cefazolin or vancomycin or clindamycin by allergy and resistance) at least four hours before delivery, newborn observation pathways, late onset untouched by this intervention.
steps.say: Four hours of penicillin before delivery rewires neonatal sepsis rates nationally.

nodes.label: Newborn observation or evaluation by algorithm

steps.tx: **GBS culture craft** uses selective enrichment (Lim broth, chromogenic media) because rectovaginal flora buries scanty GBS, susceptibility includes clindamycin testing for penicillin allergic mothers (resistance rising), and intrapartum NAAT substitutes where culture timing failed. Screening quality is an enrichment lesson wearing obstetric clothes.
steps.say: Enrich first or miss colonisation; the broth decides the prophylaxis.

right.title: Allergy pathways
points: High risk: clindamycin if susceptible and D tested

steps.tx: **PSGN versus rheumatic fever** after pyogenes is the classic fork: different strains, latencies, immune mechanisms (complex complement versus mimicry), organs (kidney versus heart joints brain), recurrence rules (PSGN rarely recurs, rheumatic fever scars by recurrence) and prophylaxis (secondary penicillin for rheumatic only). One infection, two sequela schools.
steps.say: Kidney once or heart by recurrence: sequela counselling diverges completely.

steps.tx: **GBS vaccine horizon** (capsular conjugate in maternal trials) aims to protect neonates through transferred IgG (the antibody module's placenta logic), potentially retiring screening complexity, while serotype replacement watched from pneumococcal experience counsels humility. Prevention history here is unfinished science. Until trials mature, screening and intrapartum prophylaxis remain the standard against which any vaccine must prove both safety in pregnancy and durable neonatal antibody.
steps.say: Vaccinate the mother, arm the newborn through placenta: GBS prevention's next chapter.

left.title: Vaccine promise
points: Covers early and late onset potentially

steps.tx: **Neonatal sepsis evaluation** closes the loop: early onset presentations (respiratory distress, poor feeding, temperature instability) within 72 hours demand cultures and empiric ampicillin plus gentamicin (GBS and E coli covered), lumbar puncture by condition, calculators refining observation for well term infants of treated mothers in some systems.
steps.say: A sick newborn gets cultures and ampicillin plus gentamicin before arguments about probabilities.

left.title: Early onset workup
points: GBS, E coli K1, Listeria the core threats

right.title: Observation pathways
points: Sepsis calculators (gestation, GBS, rupture, maternal fever)
Cultures still precede antibiotics when treating
